title: Hayden Panettiere death investigation closed by police in South Carolina | CNN
text:
Source: CNN

Police in South Carolina closed the investigation into actress Hayden Panettiere’s death after it was determined she died of an accidental drug overdose, the Greenville police department said Wednesday.

“Based on the (coroner’soffice’s) determination and the findings of the investigation, Hayden Panettiere’s death has been ruled accidental. The Greenville Police Department has concluded its investigation,” the police department said in an email to CNN.

The Greenville County Coroner’s Office ruled Panettiere’s deathan accidentlast month, but investigators had been looking into whether the 36-year-old obtained illicit and possibly counterfeit drugsfrom a dealer in Southern California.

Panettiere, who starred in the TV shows “Heroes” and “Nashville,” was pronounced dead at a Greenville apartment on August 16.

The actress died from a toxic mix of the opioid fentanyl and other drugs,authorities saidin September.

The Drug Enforcement Administrationhad joinedthe investigation into Panettiere’s death, and CNN has asked the agency whether its investigation remains open.

Sgt. Diana Munoz, a spokesperson for the Greenville Police Department, told CNN she couldn’t speak on whether any other agency is still looking into the death.

Panettiere was foundin cardiac arrestand medics were unable to resuscitate her. She was found in the Airbnb apartment, sitting with her legs crossed and her face down, according to a coroner’s report obtained by CNN.

Two men — later identified by police as Panettiere’s boyfriend and his brother — discovered her on a sofa bed. Panettiere was purple, the coroner’s report says. One man administered two doses of Narcan and called 911 after she remained unresponsive.

One of the men said he didn’t know Panettiere had used illegal drugs in recent days, but “she was very good at hiding them,” the coroner’s report said.

The actress had publicly shared her struggles withearly fameand herbattles with mental healthand addiction.

This year, Panettiere addressed the challenges in amemoirandspoke publiclyaboutlosing her brother.

Her career was also making a comeback, with her latest film released in January.

This story has been updated with additional information.

CNN’s Holly Yan, Deidre McPhillips, Elizabeth Wolfe and Nadia Kounang contributed to this report.
